Approach gully.notes: Scree and talus lead up from the high camp, skirting snow patches, to a narrow cairned ledge that steps into the gully. The lower gully runs under steep pale rock and is class 3-4, with one short low-5th step before it opens out. Loose rock is common.

Upper couloir.notes: Rope up near an old piton at the foot of a large chimney. A short pale slab and a rising rightward traverse on a sloping ledge follow, then two more short easy pitches finish at Black Tooth Notch.

review.changed: Wrote both boxes from one trip account (the only fetchable page); it does not use the stored labels, so mapped by order and content. Left out the stored 'black stairs' and West Tower notch wording since the account does not confirm them. No lengths stated by a source.
review.other_findings: Stored Upper couloir says the notch lies between the summit and West Tower; the account only names Black Tooth Notch. Not verified.

Lower buttress.notes: From the Mustard Glacier, solid 3rd and 4th class rock leads up to a snow patch at the foot of the face, where the party ropes up. Rockfall risk is real low on the buttress: a block that looked sound has pulled out underfoot, so test holds.

Buttress crest.notes: Parties simul-climb most of the crest in two rope teams. About a third of the way up, the line goes around a sharp prow and uses low-5th ledges to return to the crest. The ground is remote, so an injury here is serious.

review.changed: Wrote the two boxes from a single trip report of this route. No lengths or anchors stated.
